sourceFile: "2026 of Cycle of Prayer.pdf", fetched directly from https://static1.squarespace.com/static/665893c08f67ce2f2b45dddd/t/69261462ffa4475512b3e47f/1764103266858/2026%2Bof%2BCycle%2Bof%2BPrayer.pdf.
notes: The whole cycle is a single letter-size page (a Canva-designed graphic) laid out as a 4x3 grid of month boxes, each box listing several dated bullet lines -- transcribed by rendering the page as a high-resolution image and reading each month box directly against that rendering, not by trusting a linearized text extraction alone, given the multi-column-grid interleaving risk this corpus flags elsewhere.

Covers the full calendar year: 52 Sundays (January 4 - December 27, 2026) plus two fixed-date feasts the source also lists even though they don't fall on a Sunday in 2026 -- Epiphany (January 6, a Tuesday) and Christmas (December 25, a Friday). No year-boundary gap or split is needed.

The page header prints only 'Cycle of Prayer' (with '2026' as a separate large numeral); the diocesan seal printed beside it reads 'THE EPISCOPAL DIOCESE OF WISCONSIN EST. 1847' -- `diocese` is transcribed from the seal as 'The Episcopal Diocese of Wisconsin', the fullest self-identification the document itself gives.

Two dates print only a liturgical observance name with nothing else that week: Easter Sunday (April 5) and Christmas (December 25). Per this corpus's standing convention for such rows (see episcopal-new-jersey-2026.json's notes), the observance name itself is used as the sole `category` subject, since entryShape requires a non-empty `subjects` array and the source genuinely names nothing else those weeks.

The other four liturgical labels the source marks in red/bold (Epiphany Jan 6, Palm Sunday Mar 29, Pentecost May 24, Advent 1 Nov 29) are all paired with real parish subjects that week, so `liturgicalNote` is set but `subjects` holds the named parishes, not the label. All dates without a marked label carry `liturgicalNote: null`.

On May 24 specifically, the source prints 'Pentecost' running directly into the following parish name with no semicolon or comma at all ('Pentecost Christ Church Cathedral, Eau Claire; ...'), unlike the other three paired labels (Epiphany, Palm Sunday, Advent 1) which are each followed by a semicolon -- disclosed since the punctuation is inconsistent, though the parse (liturgicalNote 'Pentecost', first subject 'Christ Church Cathedral'/'Eau Claire') is not in doubt.

Several dates separate their two parishes with a comma, or with '&', instead of the semicolon used everywhere else in the source, making the parish/place split a judgment call rather than a printed certainty: June 21 ('Grace, Sheboygan, St. Alban's, Superior', parsed as Grace/Sheboygan and St. Alban's/Superior), September 6 ('Christ Church, Bayfield, St. Luke's Madison', parsed as Christ Church/Bayfield and St. Luke's/Madison -- also missing the comma before the second place), October 18 ('St. Mary's, Tomah, Holy Apostles, Oneida', parsed as St. Mary's/Tomah and Holy Apostles/Oneida), November 22 ('St. John's, Elkhorn, St. Peter's, Ripon', parsed as St. John's/Elkhorn and St. Peter's/Ripon), and December 13 ('Christ the King, Sturgeon Bay & Holy Nativity, Jacksonport', parsed as Christ the King/Sturgeon Bay and Holy Nativity/Jacksonport).

Several single parishes print their own name and place with no comma between them at all (unlike the 'Name, Place' pattern used everywhere else): February 8 ('St. Mary's Dousman', parsed as St. Mary's/Dousman), May 3 ('St. Paul's Beloit', parsed as St. Paul's/Beloit), November 8 ('St. John's Burlington', parsed as St. John's/Burlington), and November 29 ('Holy Trinity Waupun', parsed as Holy Trinity/Waupun).

November 29's second parish, 'St. Thomas & St. John's, New Richmond', is transcribed as a single parish whose own name contains '&' (a yoked/merged parish name), not as two separate parishes -- unlike the comma/'&'-separated pairs listed above, this one has only a single trailing place, supporting the single-parish reading.

Apparent misspellings preserved verbatim rather than silently corrected, per this corpus's standing rule: 'Delevan' for Christ Church's town on January 18 (the actual Wisconsin municipality is spelled 'Delavan'); 'St. Bartholowmew's' for the November 15 parish in Pewaukee (likely 'St. Bartholomew's').

November 22's own date label is printed '22rd' in the source (not '22nd'). This has no effect on the transcribed `date` field, which is 2026-11-22 -- a Sunday, consistent with the rest of the weekly pattern -- but is disclosed as a preserved-not-corrected source oddity.

Minor cosmetic inconsistencies with no effect on the transcribed data: some date labels omit the colon after the ordinal (e.g. 'March 8', 'August 9', 'May 31'), and a few lines carry stray double spaces or a stray space before a comma (e.g. 'Holy Cross , Wisconsin Dells' on September 13, 'St. Mark's , South Milwaukee' on October 25).

'St. Marc Episcopal Church' (February 8) and 'St. Marc Episcopal School' (June 28) are both recorded as `parish` subjects with `place` given as 'Jeanette, Haiti' exactly as printed -- a companion-diocese congregation and school, not a Wisconsin town. This stretches subjectShape's `place` field (documented as 'the city/town') to a town+country pair since the source gives no separate breakdown; disclosed as a judgment call.

'Parishes of the Diocese of Masvingo' (March 15) and 'The Sisters of St. Mary, Diocese of Newala' (May 10) are recorded as `category` subjects rather than `parish`, since each names a companion-diocese relationship (Masvingo, Zimbabwe; Newala, Tanzania) or a religious community, not one specific place-anchored congregation.

'St. Francis House Student Center, UW Madison & all Campus Ministers' (August 30) is recorded as a `category` rather than `parish`: 'UW Madison' is a university campus, not a town/city, and the source's own text extends beyond the center itself to 'all Campus Ministers' generally.

Two near-duplicate but distinct discernment categories appear and are transcribed exactly as printed without harmonizing the wording: 'Those discerning a call to Ordained Ministry' (May 31) and 'Those discerning a call to ordained ministry or mission work.' (December 27, including its own trailing period and lowercase 'ordained ministry').
